w:r.w:t: Existing-System Safety Audit + Controlled Android Location Foundation

The previous Sprint 01 is directionally correct, but it combines an architecture audit and implementation in the same sprint. Under the Shubh Labh project standards, the safer approach is to make Sprint 01 an AUDIT + ARCHITECTURE FREEZE sprint first. No production location tracking implementation should begin until the actual existing mobile architecture, permissions, database objects, and OnePlus/Xiaomi/Samsung device capabilities are verified.
STATUS: REVALIDATED — REQUIRES SCOPE CONTROL BEFORE DEVELOPMENT

Audit the existing Shubh Labh CRM and mobile implementation for location tracking, identify what already exists, freeze the correct architecture, and produce the exact minimal implementation plan for the next sprint. The audit must protect all existing functionality and must not create duplicate location architecture.

Establish a reliable foundation for company-controlled field-staff location records using the staff Android phones’ built-in Location Services and the existing Supabase/PostgreSQL backend, without Google Maps, paid location services, or unnecessary third-party infrastructure.
Inspect the actual mobile application technology and deployment model.
Inspect existing authentication and staff/user identity mapping.
Inspect existing Customer, Dispatch, Logistics/Transporter, Requirements, Follow-ups, Activity, and location-related functionality.
Inspect Supabase/PostgreSQL tables, views, functions, storage, APIs/Edge Functions, indexes, and RLS policies relevant to location.
Inspect existing mobile permissions and background execution handling.
Search the codebase for existing GPS/location/geolocation/background-location implementations before adding anything.
Determine whether any existing location data can be reused instead of creating new tables or fields.
Classify every relevant area as exactly one of:
MISSING — implementation required in a later approved sprint
Staff Location — where the staff device was located.
Customer Location — the customer’s stored address/location.
Dispatch/Delivery Location — where a dispatch was delivered.
Transporter Service Location — cities/areas a transporter serves.
Do not merge these concepts into one generic location table or field.
7. Proposed Staff Location Event — Validate Before Building
If no equivalent structure exists, validate the need for a minimal staff-location event structure containing:
Minimal synchronization/error metadata only if required
Do not create these fields merely because they are listed here. First confirm whether equivalent existing fields already exist.
Determine the exact Android background-location approach supported by the existing mobile application.
Determine required Android permissions and the difference between foreground and background operation.
Determine whether a foreground service/ongoing notification is required by the actual implementation and Android versions in use.
Test behaviour when the app is minimized, screen is locked, app is swiped away, device is rebooted, battery saver is enabled, and manufacturer battery restrictions are applied.
Do not implement an undocumented 'secret' background mechanism or bypass Android permission/security controls.
Document what the application can reliably capture and what the operating system/device prevents.
Use the Android phone’s built-in Location Services/GPS.
Verify every location record can be tied to an authenticated staff/user.
Verify Admin/User access rules before implementation.
Verify Users cannot read another staff member’s location history unless explicitly permitted by the existing authorization model.
Verify location endpoints cannot be accessed anonymously.
Verify no service-role or privileged Supabase credential is embedded in the mobile application.
Identify retention/deletion requirements for location data and report them for approval; do not invent a retention period in this sprint.
Determine whether the existing mobile app already has an offline queue/sync mechanism.
If it exists, plan to reuse it.
If missing, report it as a later implementation requirement rather than creating a second sync architecture in this sprint.
Validate how failed uploads will be surfaced and retried.
Inspect existing CRM UI patterns before proposing any location UI.
Do not redesign the sidebar, Today’s Work, Customer pages, Dispatch, Logistics, or other existing screens.
Identify the smallest appropriate future integration point for Admin location review.
Do not build maps in this sprint.
Do not add a new design system, UI library, or unnecessary dependency.
14. Scope Boundary — What This Sprint May Change

This sprint is primarily diagnostic. Code changes are permitted only when a tiny, reversible diagnostic change is required to verify an existing integration point. No production database migration, new location table, background tracking service, dashboard, map, geofence, or tracking workflow should be implemented in this sprint without explicit approval.
Identify actual mobile technology and application package/build.
Verify existing location-related code and database objects.
Test background behaviour on actual OnePlus device.
Test background behaviour on actual Xiaomi device.
Test background behaviour on actual Samsung device.
Verify no duplicate location architecture is required.
Run existing CRM regression checks after any diagnostic change.

Do not continue automatically after this audit. If implementation requires a new table, migration, permission model, background service, storage design, or significant mobile architecture change, report it and wait for approval.

Implement only the approved scope of this sprint. Treat the existing Shubh Labh CRM codebase, mobile application, Supabase/PostgreSQL schema, authentication, permissions, and UI system as the source of truth. Reuse existing architecture. Do not rebuild, duplicate, rename, drop, migrate, or redesign existing functionality without demonstrated need and approval. Never disable RLS. Never invent business data. Do not introduce paid/external location services. Do not bypass Android permissions or device security. Do not silently expand scope. If anything conflicts with the existing system, STOP and report the conflict.

The next sprint should be derived from this audit. It may cover the minimal approved Android location capture, background execution, offline queue/sync, and secure Supabase persistence. Exact implementation must follow the findings of this Sprint 01 rather than assumptions.
